items.q: What did AI "eat," and what must humans still own?
items.a: AI ate **tactical programming**; humans must win at **strategic programming** — architecture, scoping, interfaces, tests, codebase design. Your domain skills are the **ceiling** on what AI can do; seniors get ~**10×**, juniors a small boost.

items.q: Why obsess over the harness instead of the model?
items.a: Matt sees it as **50/50 model vs harness**. Optimize the codebase for **token spend** so cheaper models succeed — good **AX** (agent experience) overlaps good DX.

items.q: What is Grill Me, and how does it replace plan mode?
items.a: An **adversarial interview** (~4 sentences of skill): list ~10 consequential decisions and ask until **~98% shared understanding** before implementation — shared design concept beats plan-mode docs.

items.q: Why prefer procedure skills over ability skills?
items.a: Every **ability skill** description leaks into context (100 skills = 100 descriptions). Prefer **user-invoked procedures** with `disable-model-invocation` to avoid description bloat.

items.q: How does Matt run most work away from the keyboard?
items.a: Claude Code + Opus 4.8 medium locally, plus **Sand Castle** (Docker/Podman/Vercel sandboxes) and **GitHub Actions** — PR review agent, label-triggered implement (explore/implement/review on issues).
Matt thinks in **queues, not loops** — an AFK task queue (GitHub issues + labels) matches real teams better than infinite while-loops. Review the **system that produces code**, not just the code.

items.q: What should you do if skills and MCP have bloated your setup?
items.a: **Delete every skill, plugin, MCP, and CLAUDE.md** → observe the bare agent → layer **procedure skills** back intentionally; then set up AFK agents.

items.q: Does AI change what a business should do day to day?
items.a: No — still talk to customers and build prototypes. AI helps **implementation**, not idea generation; ask AI what to **remove**. Security bugs → build a **cron harness**, don't rely on frontier model serendipity.
